description: Wait for a running dev or start session to be ready. Call it for a session started with wait:false, after an extension_dev answer whose ready.status was not "ready", and for a build-only (noBrowser) session; an extension_dev answer with ready.status "ready" already carries this result, so there is nothing left to wait for. This polls the ready.json contract and reports compiled (the compiler finished), browserAttached (the runtime executor connected), and guestLoaded (the browser's own target list shows your extension). Read guestLoaded as the trustworthy load signal: it catches a silently rejected --load-extension that leaves ready.json stamped attached with empty logs. It is null when it could not be checked, for example a gecko session with no CDP port. Every result reports budgetMs and elapsedMs; on status 'timeout', call again to keep waiting on the same contract. In a noBrowser session this returns as soon as the compile lands, instead of waiting for a browser that will never attach. Every ready answer carries the ports the session bound, read from the contract: port (the dev server), controlPort (the control channel) and cdpPort (the browser's debug port on Chromium) or rdpPort (on Gecko), or debugPortNote when the session opened no debug port, so a question about ports is answered here without a shell. After a source edit, call it with for: "rebuild" (and since) to wait for the compile and reload; to wait for a condition (a model loading, an element appearing), call extension_eval with until, which repeats the eval until its value is truthy; this tool only reads. The reload stamp a rebuild wait reads (reloadedAt) needs Extension.js 4.1.34, not yet released; a project on 4.1.33 gets a brief watch for the background to reconnect instead, answering reattached, still-detached or not-stamped. Never sleep or tail the session log in a shell to wait. A browser that is running while the extension's background went idle (Safari and Firefox suspend a non-persistent background after 30 s, Chrome an idle MV3 service worker) answers status "background-asleep" with how to wake it, not "browser-gone"; a Safari WebDriver session that Safari ended answers "webdriver-session-ended" with the restart that opens a new one.

browser.description: Session browser; defaults to this project's live session. Required when the project runs sessions for more than one browser: the call is refused with the list rather than picking one.

for.description: What to wait for. "ready" (the default) waits for the session to be ready. "rebuild" waits for the compile after a source edit: until ready.json's compiledAt moves past its value at call time (or past since), then for the reload: an engine that stamps reloadedAt is waited on until that stamp also moves past its value at call time, answering reload.outcome "reloaded" with reloadKind (full, background, content, page or safari-resync) and reloadLabel; an older engine is watched briefly for the background to connect again (reattached, still-detached, or not-stamped for a content-script, page or Safari app re-sync reload, which it does not stamp). It answers status "rebuilt" with the new compiledAt, errors and reload, or status "compile-error" with the errors.

since.description: for: "rebuild" only. An ISO time: a compile stamped after it counts, so pass the compiledAt an earlier answer returned (or a time before your edit) and a rebuild that landed before this call is not missed.

timeout.description: Deprecated alias of timeoutMs, which wins when both are given.

timeoutMs.description: Wait budget for this call. Default 45000, clamped to 1000-50000 so one call stays under the client's 60s request timeout. On timeout, call again to keep waiting.

name: extension_wait
